description: Quantifying Risk Shows Value of Replacing Highway is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Louisiana Department of Transportation and Development; NOAA Office of Coast Survey; USGS, United States Geological Survey. Louisiana’s Highway 1 carries a significant fraction of the gas and oil that comes from the Gulf of America to distribution points in the United States. Faced with rising seas and sinking land, would the cost of rebuilding the road be worth the investment it required? Coverage: Louisiana (2014). The toolkit gives Louisiana as the location, 2014 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

Some roads in the state are already impassable during high tides, and the problem is expected to worsen over the coming decades.
